evals.prompt: Commit the currently staged changes only. I also have unrelated unstaged work that must stay untouched.
evals.expected_output: The workflow inspects both diffs, preserves the existing staging, and commits only the staged changes.
expectations: The workflow inspects the staged and unstaged changes before writing the message.
The workflow does not stage, unstage, or include the unrelated unstaged work.
The message describes only the staged changes.

evals.prompt: Commit all current changes. I am on main but did not say whether I want the commit there.
evals.expected_output: The workflow confirms the target branch before committing to the default branch.
expectations: The workflow detects that the current branch is the default branch.
The workflow asks whether to create a branch or commit directly to the default branch.
The workflow does not create the commit before the user chooses.

evals.prompt: Commit these dependency updates: vitest 4.1.9 to 4.1.10 and @vitest/ui 4.1.9 to 4.1.10.
evals.expected_output: The commit body lists every dependency with its old and new version.
expectations: The message uses an English conventional commit summary.
The body contains a separate bullet for vitest with both versions.
The body contains a separate bullet for @vitest/ui with both versions.
The message does not use a vague dependency-update summary in place of the package list.

evals.prompt: Give me only a subject line for the current documentation change. Do not create the commit.
evals.expected_output: The workflow returns one English conventional commit subject without requiring a body or changing Git state.
expectations: The output contains one conventional commit subject at most 50 characters long.
The workflow does not require a body because the user explicitly requested a subject-only message.
The workflow does not stage files or create a commit.

evals.prompt: Commit the current changes. The pre-commit hook failed with a lint error.
evals.expected_output: The workflow reports the exact failure and does not bypass hooks without approval.
expectations: The workflow reports the exact hook error.
The workflow offers to fix the failure or leave it for the user.
The workflow does not use --no-verify without explicit user approval.

evals.prompt: Commit the current changes with a normal message and body.
evals.expected_output: The workflow creates a conventional commit without adding agent attribution.
expectations: The message contains a conventional commit summary and concrete body bullets.
The message contains no authorship trailer.
The workflow waits for git hooks to finish naturally.

evals.prompt: Commit the current changes. This repository has pre-commit hooks that can run silently for several minutes.
evals.expected_output: The workflow runs the commit without an execution timeout and waits for Git to exit naturally.
expectations: The workflow does not set an execution timeout for git commit.
The workflow waits until Git and all hooks exit naturally.

evals.prompt: On this feature branch, commit only the current task changes in src/status.ts. That file is unstaged, while docs/other-task.md is staged for unrelated work. Keep that staging intact.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the explicit task scope without asking staged-only versus stage-all and commits only the task file.
expectations: The workflow uses the confirmed file scope without asking again.
The workflow keeps unrelated staged work out of the commit and preserves its index state.

evals.prompt: Write a commit message for the staged changes on feat/gh-42-session-cache. Issue #42 requires caching, logout invalidation, and concurrent refresh handling. This commit adds only caching. Do not create the commit.
evals.expected_output: The message can reference #42 but does not contain a closing keyword for the partial solution.
expectations: The message does not use Closes, Fixes, Resolves, or another closing keyword for #42.
The message does not claim that logout invalidation or concurrent refresh handling is implemented.
The agent leaves Git state unchanged.

evals.prompt: Commit the current changes for Jira APP-123 on a new branch, not main. The project uses fix/ branch names. The staged diff fully implements the task, which is available through Jira.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows the authorized branch choice and preserves the Jira key without using GitHub closing semantics.
expectations: The new branch starts with fix/ and contains APP-123 in its original case.
The agent does not ask again whether to commit on main.
The commit does not claim that a GitHub closing keyword will close Jira APP-123.

evals.prompt: Give me the full commit message for the staged fix on fix/gh-42-refresh-expiry in acme/app. Earlier in this session we read issue #42 and checked the exact staged diff: it rejects expired refresh tokens before creating a session and preserves valid responses, meeting both issue requirements. The staged diff is unchanged. Do not create the commit.
evals.expected_output: The message includes a closing reference to #42 and uses the existing task and diff evidence without repeating the completed investigation.
expectations: The commit body contains Fixes #42 or another supported GitHub closing reference.
The agent does not ask the user to confirm the known task or repeat the unchanged task and diff investigation.
The agent does not create a commit or change staging.

evals.prompt: The commit and push I requested earlier are complete. Fix the empty-state label in your status feature and run the relevant check.
evals.expected_output: The agent makes and checks the local correction while preserving staging and leaving commits and publication unchanged.
expectations: The agent edits and verifies the label without staging, creating a commit, rewriting history, or pushing.
The agent does not use the completed publication request as authorization for this correction.

evals.prompt: Commit the new status feature on my feature branch. Its changes are verified and uncommitted, and there is no earlier commit for this feature. The branch has an upstream.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates the scoped feature commit and leaves publication unchanged.
expectations: The agent creates an English conventional commit for the status feature.
The agent does not push or rewrite existing commits based on the commit-only request.

evals.prompt: Amend the status feature commit with the verified label correction. The status feature commit is HEAD, is not merged, and is the only outgoing commit. Keep the commit scope.
evals.expected_output: The agent folds the correction into the existing status commit without publishing it.
expectations: The agent amends the matching HEAD commit instead of leaving a separate final correction commit.
The agent does not push because only the amendment was requested.

evals.prompt: Amend your status feature with this verified label correction and push the result. On codex/status, commit a1b2c3d adds the status feature and the next commit d4e5f6a, now HEAD, independently updates test packages. Both are mine, pushed to origin/codex/status, unmerged, and within the requested publication scope. This is a non-protected branch in my repository. The remote still matches those commits.
evals.expected_output: The agent folds the correction into the earlier status commit, preserves the separate dependency commit, and safely updates only the authorized branch.
expectations: The agent targets a1b2c3d rather than amending the unrelated dependency commit at HEAD.
The agent uses a fixup and autosquash to leave one final status commit and a separate dependency commit.
The agent publishes the rewritten history with a one-ref --force-with-lease push and does not ask for permission already covered by amend and push.

evals.prompt: Commit this verified label correction to your unmerged status feature. The matching commit is a1b2c3d, titled feat(status): show clear states for pending items; HEAD d4e5f6a contains an independent dependency update. Both commits are already pushed. There is no standing instruction to rewrite history or publish, and I have only requested a commit.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a fixup for the status commit and reports that folding it into the target still needs rewrite authorization.
expectations: The agent creates a fixup targeting a1b2c3d instead of a separate final fix commit or an amendment of unrelated HEAD.
The agent keeps Git's generated fixup! subject even when the prefix makes it longer than the normal final subject limit.
The agent does not autosquash, amend, rebase, or push without matching authorization.
The agent reports the pending rewrite needed to produce one final status commit.

evals.prompt: Commit all three verified changes on this feature branch: the new status feature with its tests, an independent update of test packages, and an unrelated typo fix in the billing parser. None has an existing unmerged commit. All three will go into one PR later. The changes are in disjoint files, and there is no unrelated staging.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates three meaningful commits, keeping the status feature and its tests together, without publishing.
expectations: The agent creates separate final commits for the status feature, the independent dependency update, and the unrelated parser fix.
The feature tests remain with the feature instead of becoming a separate test-only commit.
The agent does not squash all three changes together merely because they will share a PR, and does not push.

evals.prompt: Commit the verified label correction on codex/status-label. The original status feature was merged into main last week. This branch starts from the current main, and no unmerged commit implements this correction.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a new correction commit without changing the already merged feature history.
expectations: The agent creates a new commit for the correction.
The agent does not amend, create a fixup for, or rewrite the merged feature commit.
